item.description:
Devkitty 1.0.0 (build 300)

Changes since build 299.

Build 300: Middle-click close, all editors found, website location

  • Middle-click a tab or a workspace to close it, like in other macOS apps. It asks first in the same cases as the small x button.
  • Settings > General > Editor finds all installed code editors, including Zed, Antigravity, Windsurf, Sublime Text and JetBrains IDEs.
  • The Browser list shows only real browsers, once each. The built-in choice is now called Built-in (Devkitty) and shows the Devkitty icon.
  • Double-click the empty part of the sidebar to open a new terminal.
  • The mouse Back and Forward side buttons work in the built-in browser and in HTML previews.
  • Website location: the built-in browser asks once per site. After you click Allow, Devkitty asks macOS for Location access and gives the site your location. Settings > Browser > Location shows the macOS access and lets you forget a site's answer.
  • Cmd+P opens a typed web address (like localhost:3000 or github.com) and suggests sites from Devkitty bookmarks and history. Turn it off in Settings > Browser > Links.
  • claude rc, claude remote-control and other Claude subcommands work in Devkitty terminals again.
  • The Pull Requests toolbar works in jj (Jujutsu) repositories: it finds the nearest bookmark that is not main.

Known issue: claude rc makes the cursor and its status line blink. This also happens in Ghostty 1.4.0, the terminal engine Devkitty uses.
